en: Although many mistakenly credit Jose Rizal, lawyer Ambrosio Rianzares Bautista actually authored and read the 1898 Philippine Declaration of Independence.
Many students mistakenly believe the President makes laws, but the legislative branch, specifically the Congress, actually holds the lawmaking power.
Despite the common myth of discovery, the Philippines was already inhabited by indigenous peoples long before Ferdinand Magellan arrived in 1521.
Contrary to the belief that the maya is the national bird, the Philippine eagle holds that official national title.
Although often mistakenly viewed as a national king, Lapulapu was actually just a local chieftain ruling the island of Mactan.
People often say Spain colonized the Philippines for exactly three centuries, but the actual Spanish colonial period lasted for 333 years.
While often confused as purely Tagalog, Filipino is the national language that intentionally incorporates words from other native Philippine languages.
Many wrongly think the Supreme Court creates laws, but the judicial branch's actual duty is to interpret and apply existing laws.
Unlike the common mix-up with Lapulapu, young hero Gregorio del Pilar actually died defending the Filipinos at the Battle of Tirad Pass.
Although historically linked to Magellan, the Sinulog festival actually celebrates and honors the Santo Niño, the Holy Child Jesus.
Many mistakenly believe Gregorio Y. Zara invented karaoke, but he actually invented the two-way video telephone and an improved curved-neck alcohol lamp.
People often mistakenly call all indigenous groups 'Igorots', but Igorot is a specific term referring only to the peoples of the Cordilleras.
